explanatory_strength.rationale: The contract explains the economic claim correctly and in the right units. It resists the two errors this asset class invites: it applies the Company's OpCo economic interest before the per-share division so the Continuing Equity Owners' 14.0% is never counted as Class A value, and it refuses to subtract net debt and the mezzanine preferred from a CAFD-derived value when CAFD is already struck after cash interest and cash preferred dividends. The partition of the 206,473 MMcfe proved book into 178,544 MMcfe producing and 27,930 MMcfe non-producing is the correct way to pair an owner-cash leg with a unit-NAV leg without valuing the same molecules twice. It loses a point because the whole structure is a perpetuity approximation of a finite book rather than a period-by-period distribution curve.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: Every number traces to the 424B4 and the CG&A reserve report, which is the right tier of evidence, but there is only one filing generation of it. No 10-Q or 10-K has been filed since the 2026-06-10 IPO, so nothing in the packet can be diffed against a prior period, and the reserve report has never been re-cut. The frozen adversarial review performed no filing reconciliation and the third-party cross-check indexes zero sources. Most decisive for my lens: the unbooked mineral acreage is nowhere quantified, and for a fee mineral owner that is not a rounding item.

downside_control.rationale: There is no contractual floor under this security. The distribution is undeclared, the reserves deplete on a 7.27-year producing life, and royalty revenue is an unhedged pass-through of gas price and operator drilling decisions with no operating lever available to management. The $30.643m Series B preferred sits ahead of Class A. The one genuine support is that the assets are real, saleable minerals held in fee rather than a lease that expires, which is why this is a 2 and not a 1.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: At $26.16 against a base of $5.71 the contract computes a negative 19.53% annualised return over seven years, and the high case is still negative 17.45%. Class A market capitalisation of roughly $602m plus $64.5m net debt and $30.6m preferred against a PV-10 of $293.690m is about 2.7x PV-10. Mineral companies do trade above PV-10 because the SEC deck is backward-looking and proved-only, but 2.7x with an 8.4-year proved life and no declared dividend is not a scarce-asset entry point.

claims.claim: The routed method's two legs are both now evidenced, so the route and the executed proof finally agree.
claims.evidence: valuation_contract.json economic_ownership_map carries pdp_royalty_cash_stream on owner_cash_or_dividend_discount@1.0 and non_producing_reserve_inventory on net_asset_value@1.0; valuation_route.json primary_methods is component_owner_cash_and_unit_nav.

claims.claim: The producing component cannot capitalise volume it does not own, because the decline rate is pinned to the reserve report.
claims.evidence: 178,544 MMcfe of proved developed producing reserves over 24,548 MMcfe of pro forma annual production gives a 7.27-year life and a 13.75% decline; the emitted band is -13.75% to -13.0%.

claims.claim: The gap between the contract base of $5.71 and the $26.16 market price is a disagreement about unbooked acreage and the forward gas deck, not an arithmetic error.
claims.evidence: PV-10 moved from $72.153m on 87,213 MMcfe at $2.13/MMBtu to $293.690m on 206,473 MMcfe at $3.387/MMBtu; the contract credits no volume beyond the 206,473 MMcfe proved book.

claims.claim: Distributions from this security are substantially return of capital, not earnings.
claims.evidence: Pro forma FY2025 DD&A of $36.451m against pro forma CAFD of $36.317m, and a pro forma net loss of $32.330m.

strongest_counter_explanation: WhiteHawk owns minerals in fee across the Marcellus and Haynesville, so its economic life is not the 8.4-year proved reserve life - it is however long premier operators such as EQT, Antero, Range and CNX keep drilling the acreage, which on Appalachian inventory is measured in decades. Proved reserves are a booking convention constrained by SEC rules and the five-year PUD window, not an inventory census. On that reading the correct model is a perpetual royalty on a drilling program, the observed pro forma volume change of only -4.4% (67,255 to 64,270 Mcfe/d) is the true net decline rather than the -13.75% PDP decline, and the market's roughly 2.7x PV-10 is the normal multiple for a mineral company with long unbooked inventory rather than an overvaluation. If that is right, this contract's base is too low by a wide margin and the error is mine, not the market's.
most_important_missing_fact: A quantification of unbooked mineral inventory - net royalty acres by play with undrilled location counts and operator permit or rig activity against them - so the volume beyond the 206,473 MMcfe proved book can be risked and valued instead of left at zero.
falsifiers: The first 10-Q reports net production above 67,255 Mcfe/d, which would mean the producing decline is shallower than the 13.14% to 13.75% band the reserve report implies and the owner-cash component is understated.
The FY2026 reserve report raises PV-10 above $500m, i.e. above $0.00242m per MMcfe on the current book, resetting the unit value both components rest on.
Operator permit and rig data on WhiteHawk's acreage shows a drilling program large enough to sustain volumes flat for a decade, which would falsify the finite-life framing entirely.
specialist_findings: The scarce-asset lens requires non-overlapping physical inventory, and the packet now supplies it: the two components partition the proved book with no volume counted twice and the contract reports no double_counting_flags.
PV-10 is a 10% pre-tax discounting under SEC rules, and the owner-cash component's base required return is also 10%, so the two legs are discount-rate comparable rather than accidentally divergent.

The tax bridge is handled properly for once: the $27.364m difference between PV-10 of $293.690m and the standardized measure of $266.326m is applied as a 9.32% drag on the NAV component rather than ignored.

The realization haircut of 0.40/0.55/0.70 on non-producing volumes is the weakest judgment in the NAV leg. It is a timing proxy standing in for a proper schedule of when those 27,930 MMcfe come online, and no filed document supports the specific band.
